name: Close the monthly books for pools and client portfolios
summary: Each month the investment accounting team closes the books for every investment pool and client portfolio. The custodian keeps the official accounting records, so the model manager's senior accountants reconcile the custodian's month-end figures to their own book of record, review prices, book private market and hedge fund activity, accrue manager fees and cost recovery charges, check the unitholder register against pool net assets and explain the month's movement before the director signs off. The close is slowed by waiting on the custodian for reports and corrections, by late inputs such as the cost allocation, by manual journals that the custodian has to key, and by private market information that arrives after the period is locked.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager with about 240 staff and $79 billion under management, four public equity and alternatives pools and five client portfolios holding pool units and segregated private assets, with fund accounting outsourced to a global custodian.
baseline.notes: Unit of work is one month-end close for one pool or client portfolio; nine a month at the end of 2021 (four pools and five portfolios), fewer in 2019 and 2020 when there were fewer pools and clients.

unit_of_work: one monthly close for one pool or client portfolio
trigger: Month end, followed by the custodian's preliminary month-end accounting reports for the pool or portfolio.
end_state: The director (and at quarter end the CFO) has signed off the month's net assets and the package has been released to performance, client reporting and cost allocation, with any later private market adjustment booked or the period restated.

volume.seasonality: Every month; quarter-end months add approved private valuations, CFO sign-off and quarterly client reports, and the year end adds audit requests.

evidence.note: Four pools at the end of 2021 (release) plus five client portfolios (org file); five cases a month in 2019 to 2020 with fewer pools.

Five senior accountants in the org file; the month-end close of nine pools and portfolios takes about a third of their time, the rest going to manager fee validation, audits and ad hoc work. Cost from the org file (Job Bank NOC 11100 Toronto wages deflated to 2021, plus 10% variable pay, loaded 1.35).
Approves journals and signs off every package. Cost from the org file, above the NOC 10010 Toronto median for a director.
Signs off quarter-end net assets before quarterly client reporting.
Works custodian accounting breaks raised at month end, alongside the daily reconciliation.
Explains unmatched capital calls, distributions and fees.

roles.title: Analyst, pool unit pricing and transfer agency
roles.department: Pool unit pricing and transfer agency

evidence.note: Corrects unitholder register differences for the pools.

roles.title: Analyst, budgeting, cost allocation and billing
roles.department: Financial planning, cost allocation and client billing

evidence.note: Supplies the month's cost recovery allocation by pool and portfolio when it is late.

systems.name: Custodian portal (custody, accounting records, net asset value reports, cash and corporate action notices)
Order management, pre-trade compliance and investment book of record platform (vendor software as a service)
Private markets investment accounting and monitoring system (commitments, calls, distributions, valuations)
Pool unitholder register and transfer agency records (custodian module with controlled spreadsheets)
Email, video calls and collaboration suite
Investment data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Corporate ERP (general ledger, accounts payable, budgeting)

steps.name: Custodian completes month-end accounting and issues preliminary reports
steps.description: After month end the custodian, which keeps the official accounting records and calculates pool net asset values, closes its books with final month-end prices, income accruals and exchange rates and posts preliminary trial balances, holdings, transaction and net asset reports for each pool and client account on its portal.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Fund accounting is commonly outsourced to a custodian or administrator; delivery on the second to fourth business day is an estimate.

steps.name: Download the month-end reports and load the close workbook
steps.description: The senior accountant downloads the custodian's trial balance, holdings, income and net asset reports for the pool or portfolio, loads them into the reconciliation tool and the close workbook, and opens the month's close checklist.

error.defect_description: Wrong report version or account loaded.

evidence.note: Typical oversight model where the asset manager reviews the custodian's accounting; times are estimates.

steps.name: Reconcile custodian accounting to the book of record
steps.description: The accountant matches the custodian's month-end positions, cash, market values, accrued income and pending trades against the investment book of record and the daily reconciliation results, and lists every unexplained difference above tolerance with its age and owner.

error.defect_description: A break is cleared against the wrong item and the real difference remains.

control.basis: Complementary user entity control expected by the custodian's CSAE 3416 / SOC 1 Type 2 report on fund accounting and custody, and internal control over financial reporting for the pools' audited statements: reconciliation of custodian records to the user's records with breaks resolved

evidence.note: Reconciliation of portfolio accounting to custodian records is a baseline control objective, and user-side reconciliation of returned data is a typical complementary control; break rate and times are estimates.

steps.name: Investigate breaks and query the custodian
steps.description: A reconciliations analyst traces each break to trade, corporate action, income or pricing records, decides whether the custodian or the book of record is wrong, corrects internal records, and raises queries with the custodian's client service team for its errors.

error.defect_description: Break wrongly attributed, so the wrong side is corrected.

evidence.note: Discrepancies researched and resolved in a timely manner is the baseline reconciliation objective; times are estimates.

steps.name: Custodian researches the query and posts corrections
steps.description: The custodian's fund accounting team researches the query, posts corrected trades, income or prices in its accounting system and confirms the fix, which can take several days when the item involves a sub-custodian or a complex corporate action.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Turnaround is an estimate; custodian service level agreements commonly set response times for queries.

steps.name: Review month-end prices and exchange rates
steps.description: The accountant reviews the custodian's price exception report for stale, manually overridden or unusually moved prices and differences against a second vendor, checks month-end exchange rates, and approves or challenges each exception under the pricing policy.

error.defect_description: A stale or wrong price is accepted.

control.basis: The model manager Investments Valuation Policy and Complementary user entity control expected by the custodian's CSAE 3416 / SOC 1 Type 2 report on fund accounting and custody, and internal control over financial reporting for the pools' audited statements: review of pricing exceptions and approval of overrides

next.condition: price challenge sent to the custodian

evidence.note: Valuation from an authorised source is a baseline control objective; challenge rate and times are estimates.

steps.name: Book private market and hedge fund activity and carry values
steps.description: The accountant agrees the month's capital calls, distributions and fees from the private markets system to custodian cash, records non-custodied private and hedge fund holdings at the latest approved value adjusted for cash flows, or at the new quarter's approved valuations when they have arrived, and prepares the custodian instructions.

error.defect_description: A call or distribution booked to the wrong client account or period.

evidence.note: Limited partners book call and distribution components from notices; trade date and fair value accounting per peer statements. Shares and times are estimates; client portfolios carry most private holdings in 2021.

steps.name: Private markets operations explains unmatched activity
steps.description: A private markets operations analyst checks the notice, the wire and the split across client accounts for each unmatched call, distribution or fee, corrects the private markets system where it was wrong and sends the accountant the explanation.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Handoff to private markets operations; times are estimates.

steps.name: Collect accrual inputs
steps.description: The accountant gathers the month's external manager fee accruals from fee validation, the model manager's cost recovery charge for the pool or portfolio, custody and other expense accruals, estimated hedge fund values and withholding tax reclaims, and checks that each covers the right period.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: cost allocation or fee estimate missing

evidence.note: Fees and income on an accrual basis per peer statements; late-input share is an estimate.

steps.name: FP&A provides the month's cost recovery allocation
steps.description: When it is missing, the financial planning analyst runs the month's allocation of the model manager's operating costs to each pool and client portfolio with the agreed keys, has it checked, and sends the figures and support to investment accounting.

error.defect_description: Allocation uses last month's keys.

evidence.note: Monthly cost allocation is an org file assumption; timing is an estimate.

steps.name: Prepare accrual and adjustment journals
steps.description: The accountant calculates the accruals, writes journal entries for fees, cost recovery, expenses and any corrections, attaches the support to each entry and fills in the custodian's journal instruction template for the pool or portfolio.

error.defect_description: Wrong amount, account or period on a manual journal.

evidence.note: Manual journals are named in the org file as a source of delay; times are estimates.

steps.name: Director approves the manual journals
steps.description: The director of investment accounting reviews each journal against its support, checks the accounts and period, and approves it for sending to the custodian or returns it to the preparer with questions.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: manual journals approved by someone other than the preparer before posting (COSO 2013 control activities)

evidence.note: Peer evaluates internal control over financial reporting against COSO 2013; return rate is an estimate.

steps.name: Custodian posts journals and issues final month-end reports
steps.description: The custodian keys the approved journal instructions and private holding values, reruns its month-end net asset calculation and posts the final trial balance and net asset statement for the pool or portfolio.

error.defect_description: Custodian keys a journal wrongly.

evidence.note: Custodian turnaround is an estimate.

steps.name: Review final reports, income and expense accruals
steps.description: The accountant checks that every journal posted as approved, reviews dividend and interest accruals, withholding tax and expense accruals for reasonableness against last month and the holdings, and clears or escalates anything odd.

error.defect_description: A mis-posted journal or missed accrual passes review.

control.basis: Complementary user entity control expected by the custodian's CSAE 3416 / SOC 1 Type 2 report on fund accounting and custody, and internal control over financial reporting for the pools' audited statements: review of reports returned by the service organisation

evidence.note: Investment income is a baseline control objective and user review of returned reports a complementary control; four pools and five portfolios set the branch shares.

steps.name: Reconcile the unitholder register to pool net assets
steps.description: For a pool, the accountant multiplies units outstanding in the register by the month-end unit price, compares the result with the custodian's net assets, and agrees the month's subscriptions, redemptions and switches in the register to the pool's capital activity.

error.defect_description: A small unit difference is accepted as rounding.

control.basis: The model manager unit pricing and transfer agency procedures: units on issue reconciled to net assets every pricing cycle (good practice in ASIC RG 94)

evidence.note: Reconciliations in each pricing cycle are RG 94 good practice; pooled fund unit values follow the client policy. Difference rate is an estimate.

steps.name: Unit pricing corrects the register or dealing record
steps.description: A unit pricing analyst traces the difference to a late or mis-keyed subscription, redemption or switch, corrects the register spreadsheet or custodian module with approval, and confirms the corrected units to investment accounting.

error.defect_description: Correction applied to the wrong client.

evidence.note: Register kept in a custodian module with controlled spreadsheets (org file assumption).

steps.name: Reconcile client portfolio net assets
steps.description: For a client portfolio, the accountant adds the value of the client's units in each pool to its segregated holdings and cash, agrees the month's contributions and withdrawals to the client's cash instructions, and compares the total with the custodian's account-level statements.

error.defect_description: A client cash flow is matched to the wrong month.

control.basis: Complementary user entity control expected by the custodian's CSAE 3416 / SOC 1 Type 2 report on fund accounting and custody, and internal control over financial reporting for the pools' audited statements: contributions and withdrawals agreed to client authorisations

evidence.note: Contributions and distributions authorised and recorded accurately is a baseline control objective; rates are estimates.

steps.name: Analyse the movement in net assets
steps.description: The accountant builds the bridge from opening to closing net assets (flows, income, expenses, realised and unrealised gains), compares the implied return with the performance team's preliminary figure and the benchmark, and explains every variance above the threshold.

error.defect_description: A real error is explained away as market movement.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: management analytical review of net assets before sign-off

next.condition: custodian error found, custodian corrects and reissues

evidence.note: Common analytical review practice; rates and times are estimates.

steps.name: Prepare the month-end package
steps.description: The accountant assembles the net asset statement, trial balance, reconciliations, journal list, open items with owners and dates, and the signed close checklist for the pool or portfolio, and saves it for review.

error.defect_description: Package figure does not tie to the final custodian report.

evidence.note: Typical package content; times are estimates.

steps.name: Director reviews and signs off the package
steps.description: The director of investment accounting reviews the reconciliations, open items, journals and net asset bridge, asks for explanations of anything unusual and signs off the pool's or portfolio's net assets for the month.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager financial close procedures and internal control over financial reporting: director sign-off of each pool and portfolio's monthly net assets

evidence.note: Management responsibility for internal control over financial reporting and for outsourced functions; return rate is an estimate.

steps.name: CFO signs off quarter-end net assets
steps.description: At quarter end the chief financial officer reviews the summary of net assets by pool and client, the valuation true-ups booked and open items, and signs off before quarterly client reporting and cost statements go out.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager financial reporting policy: CFO sign-off of quarter-end figures reported to clients (voluntary certification practice at peers)

evidence.note: CEO and CFO certification of internal control at a peer; the quarter-end only scope is an assumption.

steps.name: Release the package and lock the period
steps.description: The accountant files the signed package, marks the period closed in the close workbook, and notifies performance, client reporting and cost allocation that the month's net assets for the pool or portfolio are final.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: late private market information arrives after close

evidence.note: Release step; the late-information share follows the valuation workflow's true-up rate.

steps.name: Assess late private market information after close
steps.description: When a late general partner statement, a valuation true-up or a final hedge fund value arrives after the period is locked, the accountant measures its effect on the closed net assets and proposes booking it in the next month or reopening the period.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Late private market information is named in the org file as slowing the close; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Director approves reopening and the restated package
steps.description: For a material late item the director approves reopening the period, reviews the restating journal and the reissued package, and tells performance and client reporting which figures change.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: The model manager financial close procedures: reopening a closed period needs director approval

evidence.note: Common reopen control; times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Custodian accounting breaks
exceptions.description: Differences between the custodian's records and the book of record are investigated, queried with the custodian and corrected before the close can continue.

exceptions.name: Price challenge
exceptions.description: A stale or unusual month-end price is challenged and the custodian reprices.

exceptions.name: Unmatched private market activity
exceptions.description: Capital calls, distributions or fees do not agree to custodian cash and private markets operations has to explain them.

exceptions.name: Late cost allocation or fee estimate
exceptions.description: The cost recovery allocation or a manager fee estimate is missing, so the close waits for FP&A.

exceptions.name: Register difference
exceptions.description: Units in the register times the unit price do not agree to pool net assets and unit pricing corrects the register.

exceptions.name: Reopened period
exceptions.description: A material late private market item leads the director to reopen the closed month and reissue the package.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month end to the signed and released month-end package
benchmarks.population: Canadian institutional asset managers overseeing custodian fund accounting for pools and client portfolios with private assets

evidence.note: Author estimate: the custodian's preliminary reports take two to four business days, and the review, journal and sign-off stages take about as long as the cross-industry close from trial balance to statements (APQC median 6.4 calendar days, bottom quartile 10 or more), plus custodian reposting time.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from trial balance to consolidated statements
benchmarks.population: APQC Open Standards Benchmarking, 2,300 organisations (as cited, 2018)

evidence.note: Quartile labels: p25 is the top performer threshold and p75 the bottom performer threshold.

benchmarks.population: The model manager at the end of 2021

evidence.note: Four pools plus five client portfolios.

pain_points.description: The close waits on the custodian twice, for the preliminary reports and again to key journals and reissue final reports, and custodian queries take days to resolve.

evidence.note: Outsourced fund accounting stays the operator's responsibility; waits are estimates.

pain_points.description: Manual journals for fees, cost recovery and corrections are prepared in spreadsheets, approved by email and re-keyed by the custodian.

evidence.note: Named in the org file as a cause of slow closes.

pain_points.description: Private market activity and values arrive late and in many formats, so holdings are carried at stale values and adjusted after the period is locked.

evidence.note: Org file names late private market information; ILPA templates aim to standardise notices.

pain_points.description: Accrual inputs from other teams (cost allocation, fee estimates, hedge fund values) are often late, holding up the journals.

evidence.note: Author estimate of common practice.

pain_points.description: One director approves every journal and signs every package, so sign-off queues at peak days.

evidence.note: Org file has one director and no manager layer in investment accounting.

assumptions: The custodian keeps the official accounting records and calculates net assets for pools and client accounts; the model manager oversees and adjusts them through journal instructions, as the org file assumes a single custodian and fund accounting provider.

Controls in the custodian's own processing are relied on through its annual CSAE 3416 or SOC 1 Type 2 report, which the model manager reviews once a year with a bridge letter for the gap to year end; that annual review is not modelled per close. The monthly steps that the report expects user entities to perform (reconciliation, review of returned reports, price exception review, authorisation of cash flows) are marked as controls.
Pools are four of the nine monthly closes and client portfolios five; private assets sit mainly in client portfolios in 2021 because only public equity and alternatives were pooled.
Manager fee validation, capital call processing and cost allocation are separate processes that feed this close; only the follow-up when their output is late or unmatched is modelled here.
Quarter-end months add CFO sign-off on a third of closes; the CFO step is an assumption, as the model manager's sign-off hierarchy is not public.
The org file shows no manager between the director and the five senior accountants, so the director approves journals and signs off packages; this may overstate the director's load.
Loaded costs per hour are taken unchanged from the org file (wage plus variable pay times a 1.35 loading).
